title: A personalization endpoint that deserializes page state before it authenticates, and a stolen machine key that outlives the patch
index_line: T-0072 · EXEC · an unauthenticated POST reaches the page-personalization endpoint; the page lifecycle deserializes control state in-process; the machineKey then signs zero-auth persistence · dotnet · corroborated
invariant_violated: SharePoint's page-personalization endpoints assumed only authenticated users could reach them, and the page lifecycle assumed anything already parsing control state had been let in. Neither survived one crafted unauthenticated POST — and once the machineKey was read out, patching the code no longer revoked the signature the attacker now owned.

mechanism.does: a crafted POST to the layout-personalization endpoint arrives with no session (the observed wave also carried a SignOut.aspx Referer)
the personalization path's access control misses the request — the endpoint processes an unauthenticated caller (CVE-2025-49706)
the page lifecycle parses server-side control state from the request and instantiates attacker-named types in the web application process (CVE-2025-49704) — the initial RCE needs no file write
the injected objects execute in-process; web shells dropped afterwards are persistence variants, not the mechanism
post-exploitation shells read the ASP.NET machineKey/ValidationKey; ysoserial then mints validly-signed __VIEWSTATE payloads — zero-authentication RCE that survives the patch until keys are rotated

source.http.body.value: the crafted POST body to the layouts endpoint — page state the lifecycle will deserialize

guard.none.value: no check between the personalization surface and the page lifecycle's object instantiation; after key theft, no credential at all — only a valid signature

sink.deser.native.value: the page-lifecycle control-state deserialization in the web application process

gadget.magic-method.value: instantiation of attacker-named types (TypeConfuseDelegate-style ViewState gadgets once the key is held)

preconditions.expr: the layouts endpoint answers (the platform returns 200 even where files are absent — treat as surface, not proof)
an on-prem build in the vulnerable window, unpatched past 2025-07-08
an ASP.NET machineKey exists in the farm configuration — the persistence leg depends on it

success: an unauthenticated POST to the layouts endpoint executes in the web application process (observed: whoami and cmd.exe chains under the w3wp process)
web shells that print the machineKey configuration fields (ValidationKey/Validation/DecryptionKey/Decryption/CompatibilityMode)
a ysoserial-signed __VIEWSTATE payload executes commands on any request with zero authentication — and keeps working after the code is patched, until keys rotate
failure_like: the 2025-07-08 patch and the bypass fixes (CVE-2025-53770/53771) applied
AMSI in Full Mode blocks the unauthenticated in-memory attack path
false_positive: valid credentials in use would be a different intrusion — this chain uses none
a signed-ViewState PoC without the key presumes what this chain earns first; the record's order is bypass, then deserialization, then key theft

hazards: every 'authenticated users only' personalization or maintenance page — the class is a control-plane surface that parses state before it re-checks identity
the machineKey is the real persistence: rotate keys and restart IIS after any suspected compromise; patching alone leaves the attacker a valid signer

adoption was immediate and wide: two named state actors plus a ransomware-deploying cluster exploited it from 2025-07-07; over 400 compromised servers and 8,000+ internet-facing instances at disclosure
the initial chain runs in-memory with no file drop — assume other unlogged variants exist
non_transfers: the hosted/SaaS variant of the platform (not on-prem)
farms with the patches applied and keys rotated after every suspected exposure

evidence.target: Microsoft SharePoint Server on-prem (ToolShell: CVE-2025-49706 + CVE-2025-49704; bypass variants CVE-2025-53770/53771; mass-exploited from 2025-07-07)

provenance.author: Eye Security
provenance.corroborates: the exploited chain and its correction: ToolShell (CVE-2025-49706 auth bypass + CVE-2025-49704 deserialization RCE, demonstrated at Pwn2Own Berlin by Code White); in-memory execution with no file write; machineKey/ValidationKey theft web shells; ysoserial-signed ViewState persistence surviving patching; 400+ compromised, 8,000+ exposed; 2025-07-29 correction clarifying 53770/53771 are patch bypasses

provenance.author: Microsoft Threat Intelligence
provenance.corroborates: vendor account: POST-based exploitation of the ToolPane endpoint from 2025-07-07 by Linen Typhoon, Violet Typhoon and Storm-2603 (Warlock/Lockbit ransomware); spinstall*.aspx shells that retrieve MachineKey data; AMSI Full Mode and machine-key rotation + IIS restart as mitigation; 53770/53771 fix the bypasses of 49704/49706
